item.content:encoded:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.

item.content:encoded:
Blake Snell exits Dodgers’ loss early because of injury
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — The trouble started as Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell threw in the Great American Ball Park bullpen before the game.
“I felt good all day, and then the second-to-last pitch of the bullpen, I threw a slider and then I felt it grab,” Snell said of the groin tightness that ended up taking him out of the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds early. “So I was like, ‘Alright, let’s see what we can do.’”
With Snell guiding the ball without driving hard off his back leg, his velocity was down a tick or two through a 19-pitch first inning. He gave up one hit, a single to Sal Stewart, which he quickly erased with a successful pick-off that caught Stewart in an inning-ending run-down.
“I was going to try to get through five [innings],” he said, “but I just knew I didn’t really have a good shot at doing that and remaining healthy.”
In a conversation with manager Dave Roberts, pitching coach Mark Prior and head athletic trainer Thomas Albert, they all agreed the best course of action would be to pull Snell from the game. Right-handed reliever Blake Treinen replaced him in the second inning.
With only 10 games left in the season, it’s unclear when Snell will be ready to pitch again.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
The Dodgers’ loss marked Snell’s eighth start of the season. His 2026 debut was delayed by shoulder fatigue. And then after one start, he landed back on the injured list to undergo arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow.
Since returning, he hasn’t given up more than one run in a start. Through Wednesday, Snell has a 1.86 ERA. And he’s a key member of the Dodgers’ projected postseason rotation.
“I don’t think anyone can sit here right now and say what’s going to happen in the next week to 10 days,” Roberts said, noting that the team would decide whether to send him to get imaging after they returned to Los Angeles. “It’s under the, ‘I’m glad it’s not worse and we caught it early’ [category].”
Snell has a history of left groin and adductor strains. He spent time on the IL in 2021, 2022 and 2024 for such injuries. He said this injury didn’t feel nearly as severe as any of those.
“[In the past] I felt like that and then I kept pitching on two of them and strained both of them,” he said. “One was a grade one, one was a grade two. So I’m definitely happy I stopped. … I’m aware if I kept pitching, I definitely would’ve strained it. So for me to stop, that’s a first. Maybe I’m growing up. I don’t know. But that was definitely the right move. And next couple days, we’ll see where we’re at and go from there. But I think I’ll be good to go.”
The last couple years, in an effort to avoid another groin strain, Snell has incorporated Copenhagen planks into his routine, strengthening the area.
“I thought I had this thing figured out,” Snell said. “Well, technically, I still do. I didn’t strain it, so that was a good thing. … I haven’t felt it at all until that pitch in the bullpen, and I was just kind of thrown off by it. So I’ve done what I’ve needed to do to be strong and healthy. Definitely a shock to me.”
After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

item.title: [New York Post] Blake Snell departs early and Dodgers’ rotation suddenly a question mark
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani’s aching right arm. Freddie Freeman’s throbbing right knee. Edwin Díaz’s disastrous form on a minor-league rehabilitation assignment.
Whatever problems surfaced in recent weeks, the Dodgers were able to convince themselves they could overcome them.
The reason: Even with Ohtani unable to pitch, they had the most talented starting rotation of this era.
Suddenly, that source of comfort is a major concern.
Blake Snell departed his start in Cincinnati on Wednesday after just one inning with what was described as a tight left groin.
Consider that Tyler Glasnow traveled directly home from Miami rather than to follow the Dodgers to Great American Ball Park for their four-game series against the Reds, and there are reasons to be worried.
Very worried.
With an inconsistent offense and combustible bullpen, the Dodgers were going to be heavily dependent on their starting pitching in the playoffs.
That rotation could now be unraveling.

The last time Snell strained his left groin was when he was pitching for the San Francisco Giants in 2024. He was sidelined for a month.
For what it’s worth, Snell is convinced this particular injury isn’t severe and plans to make his next start, according to people familiar with this situation.
“Stopped before it got too bad,” one of the people said.
Then again, weren’t similar claims once made about Ohtani?
As for Glasnow, he remains on track to pitch on Friday.
Manager Dave Roberts said Glasnow skipped the Cincinnati leg of the trip to better prepare for his starting assignment at Dodger Stadium against the San Francisco Giants.
“Get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time,” Roberts said.
By sending Glasnow back to Los Angeles, the Dodgers spared him a three-hour flight from Miami to Cincinnati.
Glasnow was sidelined for 3 ½ months because of back problems, and Roberts intimated something could be wrong with him after his most recent start. In his last two appearances, the 6-foot-8 right-hander gave up a combined eight runs, 11 hits and seven walks in 10 innings.
The questions about Snell’s and Glasnow’s health came at a time when the rotation was coming together before the postseason.
Snell in particular was sharp after returning from an elbow cleanup that cost him three months. Before his early departure on Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 earned-run average since he was activated from the injured list on Aug. 11.
Snell wasn’t the only Cy Young Award-caliber pitcher rounding into shape.
The day before Snell scaled the mound, it was Yamamoto’s turn to do so, and last year’s World Series Most Valuable Player pitched seven scoreless innings in a 4-0 win over the Reds.
The seven-inning start was the third in a row for Yamamoto, who improved his record to 14-8 and lowered his earned-run average to 2.51.
“I feel really good and I don’t have any physical problems,” Yamamoto told reporters in Japanese. “I want to treat practice each and every day with importance and go into October in the best condition.”
The opening game of the series was started by Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the trade deadline.
Skubal pitched seven scoreless innings of his own in a 4-1 victory over the Reds. In his previous start, which was also against the Reds but at Dodger Stadium, Skubal pitched 7 ⅓ innings.
“Just getting in a rhythm,” Skubal said.
Just last week, the Dodgers had a playoff rotation that would have looked to other teams like the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.
Now, there’s a chance they could be forced to send Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan to the mound in playoff games.
The Dodgers could conceivably win a championship with a rotation of Yamamoto, Skubal, Sasaki and Sheehan but that would require their offense to be productive.
How much can the Dodgers count on that, considering the physical problems Ohtani and Freeman have encountered? And how would using Sasaki as a starter instead of a reliever affect their bullpen?
Snell removed himself from his start on Wednesday so the Dodgers wouldn’t have to find out. The question is whether he did so in time. Their season depends on it.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell has exited Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after one inning in a concerning development with less than two weeks to go in the regular season.
Snell pitched a scoreless first inning with one strikeout across 19 pitches. There didn't appear to be anything noticeably wrong with him during the frame, but his fastball velocity was down.
At the conclusion of the first inning, Snell went down to the clubhouse alongside team trainer Thomas Albert.
Now, he's out of the game, with right-hander Blake Treinen replacing him in the bottom of the second inning.
What is Blake Snell's Injury?
The Dodgers announced Snell was removed from the game with left groin tightness.
Manager Dave Roberts will provide a more substantial update after the game, which will include whether or not Snell will need to go on the injured list.
Dodgers Can't Afford a Blake Snell Injury Right Now
Snell opened the year on the IL as he recovered from shoulder inflammation that dated back to last year. He returned for one start in May before going right back on the IL to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
He missed another three months before returning in August, and has been absolutely dominant ever since.
Entering Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts since coming off the IL. Including Wednesday's scoreless first inning, he has 47 strikeouts over 35.2 innings and hasn't allowed a home run in that stretch.
The Dodgers are relying on Snell and fellow superstar pitchers Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal to carry them in October. Thus, the team will hope Snell isn't dealing with anything serious moving forward.
Who Will Replace Blake Snell in Dodgers Rotation if He's Forced to Miss Time?
The Dodgers' starting rotation is dealing with an onslaught of injury concerns as the season winds down.
While the rotation is led by Yamamoto and Skubal (who underwent midseason elbow surgery while with the Detroit Tigers), behind them is a bunch of question marks.
Tyler Glasnow has struggled since returning from a nearly four-month absence due to a back injury. Justin Wrobleski has been removed from the rotation amid his forearm injury and struggles. Roki Sasaki is currently on the IL with a blister. Eric Lauer is out for the season due to an elbow injury.
Then there's Shohei Ohtani, who won't return as a pitcher this year (and may not even be 100% as a hitter).
The Dodgers recently demoted Emmet Sheehan, but could recall him if Snell goes on the IL. He was sharp over his two September starts, allowing one run over 11.2 innings.
If Snell isn't forced to miss time, the Dodgers will take a big sigh of relief knowing their superstar trio in the starting rotation is intact with October looming. If he's forced to go on the IL, though, it will be yet another massive blow in the team's chances to three-peat.

item.content:encoded:
The colloquially called “Great American Small Park” has looked awfully big for the Cincinnati Reds hitters facing the best pitching that the Dodgers have to offer. And it doesn’t get much easier with Blake Snell taking the mound, as the Dodgers are one win away from sweeping the Reds in a fourth straight series dating back to last year—counting both the regular season and playoffs.
Considering Sunday’s loss to the Marlins in which Emmet Sheehan pitched quite well, Dodger starters have held opponents scoreless through 20 innings, 14 of which have come against starters Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. On top of being dominant, Skubal and Yamamoto share the fact that they deviated somewhat from their regular approach in their last outing against the Reds, but in opposite directions—Skubal leaning more heavily on the fastball, while Yamamoto threw it even less than he normally does.
A critical distinction must be made between these two previous starters and Snell. Unlike the pair, Snell will be facing the Reds for the first time this season since he was not on the schedule in the three-game series at Dodger Stadium last week. And speaking of a track record against the Reds, Snell will have fond memories of his last time pitching at this stadium. Back in 2024, still with the Giants, Snell delivered one of the greatest outings of his career when he shut out the Reds in a 3-0 win—the two-time Cy Young winner punched out 11 in what, to this day, remains the only complete game and the only shutout of Snell’s illustrious career.

- Ballpark: Great American Ball Park, Cincinnati

- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

Wrobleski struck out a batter and allowed two hits and one walk over two scoreless innings of relief in Saturday's 4-3 loss to the Marlins.
After making his previous appearance as a starter Sept. 6 versus the Nationals, Wrobleski shifted back to the bullpen for the Dodgers' weekend series in Miami. He ended up being called upon Saturday in relief of starter Tyler Glasnow, who was chased after yielding four runs across four innings. Assuming the Dodgers elect to maintain a six-man rotation through the end of the season, Wrobleski could have a chance to start or pitch bulk innings again next weekend versus the Giants. The Dodgers reopened a rotation spot after optioning Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.

item.content:encoded:
By Field Level Media
Sep 15 (Field Level Media) – The Los Angeles Dodgers put relief pitcher Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list due to lower back discomfort on Monday, ending the right-hander’s regular season and causing more upheaval for the team’s bullpen.
Los Angeles has also been nursing Edwin Diaz back in a slow recovery from right elbow surgery with recent Triple-A outings that have not proven successful.
In his most recent appearance for Oklahoma City, Diaz struggled through two- thirds of an inning on Sunday, allowing five runs and three walks in a performance that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted wasn’t going to be enough to merit a promotion.
The Dodgers have left open the possibility for Henriquez to return in the postseason.
Henriquez, 24, has appeared in 61 games (one start) this season, posting a 2.85 ERA with 71 strikeouts against 25 walks in 60 innings.
Diaz, a three-time All-Star, has struggled this season in limited action, logging seven saves in 11 opportunities and an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances.
Los Angeles recalled right-handed pitchers Paul Gervase and Bobby Miller from Triple-A to help shore up their shaky bullpen. Emmet Sheehan was sent to Oklahoma City after throwing six shutout innings in a start against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
Gervase, 26, has a 2.35 ERA over four major league appearances this season. He owns a lifetime 3.38 ERA with no decisions in 10 outings, all in relief, for the Tampa Bay Rays (2025) and Los Angeles (2025-26).
Miller, 27, has made one big-league appearance in 2026, earning a win over the Washington Nationals on Sept. 6 with three innings of one-run relief. He is 14-8 with a 5.40 ERA in 38 outings (36 starts) for the Dodgers over parts of four seasons.
Sheehan, 26, is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 starts this year, 15-12 with a 4.23 ERA in 50 career appearances (45 starts), all with Los Angeles.
(–Field Level Media)

- Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” from the closer to put him on the playoff roster.
- The Dodgers placed reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list and recalled Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase.
CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on Monday, bullpen uncertainty loomed.
When they get to the playoffs, who’s going to take the ball in high-leverage situations?
Their options are dwindling. Edgardo Henriquez landed on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ruling him out for the rest of the regular season. Edwin Díaz was so shaky in his rehab assignment Sunday that a spot on the postseason roster isn’t guaranteed.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers opened a four-game series against the Reds. “So my bet is that he will be [on the roster]. But there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us to sort of bet on. And so my bet is, yes, but we’ve still got to see something.”
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
Díaz (neck) had the worst outing of his triple-A rehab assignment, surrendering five runs and issuing two walks in two-thirds of an inning. The dud put his return timeline in doubt. His next rehab appearance is scheduled for Wednesday.
“I think the world of him, the baseball card looks great,” Roberts said. “But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
So, who’s still in play?
Tanner Scott remains Roberts’ go-to in save situations. And Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Jack Dreyer and Blake Treinen all have experience in late innings.
On Monday, starter Tarik Skubal gave the group a much-needed break with seven shutout innings. He limited the Reds to three hits and a walk, cruising through their lineup almost three times in 90 pitches.
The Dodgers pulled ahead by four runs, on home runs from Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, who have both broken out of slumps, and an RBI single from Kiké Hernández.
With the game still relatively tight, Vesia entered in the bottom of the eighth to face the left-handed heavy bottom of the order. He retired the side.
Phillips and Treinen both were warming in the ninth when the Dodgers got a runner to second base with one out. When they failed to score him, Phillips jogged in to face the top of the order. He surrendered a high-flying solo homer to Elly De La Cruz on a fastball above the zone but avoided further damage.
Before the game, the Dodgers added two fresh arms to the bullpen. They recalled right-handers Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase, as they put Henriquez on the IL and optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan.
Henriquez will undergo imaging on the area, which Roberts said stretched to his side near his oblique.
“The hope is we’ll get him back in the postseason,” Roberts said.
Roberts said he didn’t know what the move meant for Sheehan, who in his past two starts limited opponents to one run and recorded 15 strikeouts in a combined 11 ⅔ innings.
“Some of it’s probably contingent on Roki [Sasaki], and we’ve got another start coming up down the road here, as far as a bullpen kind of situation,” Roberts said. “So I don’t know, but Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. The last two have been really good.”
Sasaki (right middle finger blister) could start Thursday. His bullpen session Monday marked the first time he had tested covering the sensitive area on his finger with Dermabond, Roberts said.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers also have more bullpen reinforcements coming.
Another bullpen addition is left-hander Kris Bubic, who met the team in Cincinnati and is in place to make his Dodgers debut later this week. Bubic made his last rehab appearance for triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so Roberts said the Dodgers likely won’t activate him off the 60-day injured list until Wednesday at the earliest.
The Dodgers acquired Bubic from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline this year. He’d been on the IL since May, first with a low-grade flexor strain in his left forearm, and then a shoulder impingement setback.
In six triple-A rehab appearances over 5⅔ innings, Bubic didn’t yield a run and he limited opponents to two hits and two walks.
Roberts was noncommittal about Bubic being a high-leverage option.
“Seems like all of our games are leverage these days,” he said.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
The fresh arm express continues to run in September, with Emmet Sheehan optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City ahead of Monday night's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park, one day after he pitched six scoreless innings on Sunday in Miami.
Paul Gervase was called up from Triple-A to give the Dodgers an extra arm in the bullpen, after the Dodgers used four relievers Friday, three on Saturday, and four more on Sunday against the Marlins. Monday is the fourth day of a stretch of 10 game days in a row for the Dodgers, their final extended stretch of games this season.
This had nothing to do with Sheehan's performance, as he allowed only one run in 11 2/3 innings last week after getting called back up from Oklahoma City himself, with 15 strikeouts. But Sheehan is on the outside looking in when it comes to the Dodgers' postseason rotation, and the team might also get Roki Sasaki at some point this week from a blister on his right middle finger.
Gervase last pitched on Friday for Oklahoma City, striking out four in a four-out save in a scoreless outing to close out a win over Sugar Land. On the season, the 6'10 right-hander had a 4.56 ERA and five saves in 38 games in Triple-A, with 66 strikeouts and 35 walks in 47 1/3 innings.
This is the fifth stint in the majors this season for Gervase, who has a 2.35 ERA in four appearances for the Dodgers, with eight strikeouts and five walks in 7 2/3 innings.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A in a surprise move ahead of Monday's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds.
Sheehan has been dominant over his last two starts since returning to the MLB level, allowing a combined one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
However, the Dodgers wanted to bring up a fresh bullpen arm for the beginning of their four-game series in Cincinnati. Thus, Sheehan was the odd man out, with right-handed pitcher Paul Gervase being called up.
Dodgers Option Emmet Sheehan
Sheehan has had a rollercoaster 2026 season that began with much promise. However, the right-hander struggled across his first 20 starts, and was optioned to Triple-A on Aug. 3 after allowing five runs on six hits over 2.2 innings against the Boston Red Sox.
At the time of the demotion, Sheehan's ERA was 5.29. However, he played well across four Triple-A outings and earned another opportunity at the MLB level on Sept. 7 against the Reds.
Sheehan allowed one run over 5.2 innings with a tied-for-career-high 10 strikeouts against Cincinnati. That led to him staying in the rotation for another turn, where he dominated the Marlins on Sunday.
Sheehan is now ineligible to return to the Dodgers before the end of the regular season barring an injury to someone else that would allow him to be called back up.
He'll look to continue to keep his game strong ahead of the postseason, where he could still factor into the team's plans.
“There was a lot of stuff, going down and trying to figure things out in a less stressful place which was nice,” Sheehan said after his start on Sept. 7. “Just getting my delivery locked in and really just making sure I’m hammering it during the week so I can just go out there and compete which I felt I was doing tonight.”
"I’ve been optioned before," he added. "It’s always, 'See what we can do down there, and see what we can do to bring it back up here.'"
Now, he'll have to do that once more.
Dodgers Calling Up Paul Gervase
As for Gervase, the right-hander has made four appearances for the Dodgers at the big league level this season, allowing two runs over 7.2 innings for a 2.35 ERA with eight strikeouts.
Across 38 appearances at Triple-A Oklahoma City, he has a 4.56 ERA with 66 strikeouts over 47.1 innings.

item.content:encoded:
MIAMI –– The Dodgers’ bullpen melted down once again on Sunday in Miami.
Only this time, they got an unhelpful hand from some shaky late-game defense.
In a 6-4 loss to the Miami Marlins, the Dodgers allowed all of the scoring in the final two innings of what became a walk-off defeat; watching three high-leverage relievers –– Edgardo Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Brock Stewart –– falter after their infield gave away extra outs behind them.
In Henriquez’s two-run eighth inning, one would-be groundout instead snuck between shortstop Mookie Betts and second baseman Miguel Rojas, leaving Rojas injured after he made a late sliding attempt. Another got stuck in Betts’ hand while he tried to make a charging throw on the run, gifting the Marlins a free scoring opportunity that would lead to a two-run single from Otto Lopez.
The four-run ninth inning, which was capped off by Agustín Ramírez’s walk-off homer against Stewart, was just as frustrating, as Scott’s bid for a four-out save imploded after a pair of infield singles; one on a bunt, and another on a bad underhand flipped from a hobbled Freddie Freeman at first base.
“When you give a team extra outs,” manager Dave Roberts said, “that’s what happens.”
Initially, it appeared as though the Dodgers might still escape.
After Lopez’s single in the eighth, Scott replaced Henriquez to face Griffin Conine and struck him out on three pitches to end the inning and keep a 3-2 lead intact.
In the top of the ninth, the Dodgers added to the advantage on Betts’ RBI double, giving them “enough to win” offensively, as Roberts put it, even though they left the bases loaded later in the frame.
Alas, the bottom of the ninth immediately went sideways on an Xavier Edwards ground ball to lead off the inning.
Freeman, who has been playing through a knee injury and is mired in a 1-for-26 slump, fielded the ball but made a bad underhand flip back to first. Scott had to adjust to it as he went to cover the base, and was too late to recover as Edwards beat the play out.
Jakob Marsee came up next and executed a perfect bunt inside the third-base line.
Then, Javier Sanoja got jammed by a slider but still muscled a two-run double into the left-field corner.
Just like that, the Dodgers’ lead was gone. It was only Scott’s fourth blown save in 26 opportunities this season, but also the sixth time in his last 11 outings he has given up a run.
“Actually, I think the last week has been really good as far as the stuff,” Roberts said when asked of that trend, which has pushed Scott’s ERA to 2.91. “Today I think was just an odd day.”
Four pitches later, the game was over. Stewart came in to face the pinch-hitting Ramírez, but grooved him a fastball that was launched to left for the walk-off blast.
“It was supposed to be up above the zone. That’s where my fastball plays best,” Stewart said. “Just missed my spot, threw it right down the middle.”
Thus, the Dodgers suffered a loss that wasted big days from Emmet Sheehan (who threw six scoreless innings in his start) and Josue De Paula (who mashed a monstrous three-run home run in the fourth inning for his first career hit), while also delaying any possibility of clinching a playoff spot for a second-straight day.
“It’s baseball,” Roberts said. “It sucks. It feels bad. But that’s part of the thing.”
With a sigh, he later added: “But yeah, today was a crappy one.”
